title: Launchpad career track: compact onboard & evaluation slate
content:
Purpose
----
Compact onboarding + evaluation template for the Launchpad (early-career / fast-embed) cohort. Designed to: shorten time-to-impact, make mentor commitments explicit, create objective signals at 14/30/60/90 days for go/no-go decisions, and reduce variance between hiring managers. This is intentionally lean — intended for small squads and satellite hires who need a high-touch 30-day acceleration followed by a structured assessment.

Context and scope
----
- Use for IC1/IC2-equivalent early-career engineers, data engineers, and technical PMs that are part of Launchpad cohort.
- Works as companion to the standard onboarding handbook; this is the compact version managers follow for fast trials.
- Not a replacement for full role competency ladders; this is an activation + assessment slate to make rapid decisions and clear support commitments.

High-level timeline (compact)
----
Day 0: hardware/software access, buddy assigned, 1:1 with manager (30m), cohort welcome (60m)
Day 1–7: quick wins lab (two small tickets), infrastructure walkthrough, safety/infra checklist, first mentor pairing session
Day 8–14: first deliverable (README + PR), 14-day sync & soft-signal check, create evaluation notes in shared dossier
Day 15–30: project ramp, cross-team introductions, shadow rotations (obs), 30-day checkpoint decision (red/yellow/green)
Day 31–60: expand scope, measurable feature/bug work, 60-day milestone review and formal rubric scoring
Day 61–90: independent ownership, final 90-day hire-readiness decision & calibration meeting with People Ops

Manager pre-boarding checklist (before Day 0)
----
- Confirm access: GitHub, CI, Jira/Linear, Slack, internal docs (list exact repos and projects).
- Assign buddy and mentor (buddy = peer for day-to-day; mentor = 1:1 technical coach).
- Draft 30-day goal (1 deliverable) and 90-day success criteria; add to candidate dossier.
- Schedule recurring 1:1s for first 8 weeks (weekly recommended).
- Add new hire to Launchpad cohort calendar and invite to weekly office hours.

Buddy / Mentor roles (explicit)
----
Buddy (day-to-day): triage small infra friction, pair on first ticket, join first three standups.
Mentor (technical coaching): weekly 45m check-ins, review rubric artifacts, advocate in calibration meeting, provide concrete growth actions.
Commitment: buddy = 1 hour/day for week 1, mentor = 1 x 45m/wk for first 8 weeks.

14/30/60/90 signals and artifacts (what to collect)
----
Signal types (quick list): ownership, code quality, cross-team communication, learning velocity, curiosity/problem diagnosis.
Artifacts to attach to dossier: first PR link, README deliverable, a short 14-day manager note (bullet list), 30/60 rubric pdf/notes, feedback snippets from peers.
Scoring snapshot at 30/60/90 (manager + mentor): Red = needs rescue / extension; Yellow = light coaching & conditional continuation; Green = on track.

Core compact rubric (use numbers 1–4; write short evidence bullets)
----
1) Problem decomposition (1–4) — evidence: ability to split task, ask clarifying Qs, write plan.
2) Code quality & deliverable (1–4) — evidence: PR review comments, tests, documentation.
3) Collaboration & communication (1–4) — evidence: meeting prep, async updates, Slack signal.
4) Autonomy & learning velocity (1–4) — evidence: ramp time, independent debugging, proactive follow-ups.
5) Reliability / craft (1–4) — evidence: shipping on time, following rollout/runbook.
Scoring guidance: 3+ consistently = likely keep; 2 = conditional with explicit remediation plan; 1 = escalate to people-ops for review.

30-day checklist (manager + mentor)
----
- Deliverable: first feature/bug + accompanying README or design note.
- 30-day meeting: manager + mentor + HR rep optional (15m).
- Items to review: rubric scores, artifacts, peer feedback, access blockers.
- Outcome options: continue as trial with target goals, extend trial (30-day extension), or offboard.

Decision ladder / recommended actions by signal
----
Green (most signals at 3–4): continue to normal onboarding, increase autonomy targets.
Yellow (mixed signals, average ~2): create explicit 30-day remediation plan: 2–3 focused outcomes, weekly checkpoints, mentor-owned mini-sprint.
Red (several signals at 1): escalate immediately, freeze progression, prepare offboard or extended support plan with people-ops.

14/30 remediation template (copy into dossier)
----
- Problem areas: (bullets)
- Specific outcomes (2–3): e.g., ship X with Y quality metrics, reduce PR cycle time by 20%
- Owner(s): manager, mentor, person
- Checkpoints: weekly meeting dates
- Consequence of not meeting outcomes: extension, role change, or offboard

Manager tips / quick heuristics (notes)
----
- Small wins early are cheap signals. If they can ship a README + test PR in 7–14 days they can usually be coached.
- Avoid confirmation bias: solicit two peer signals (different teams) rather than rely solely on manager impression.
- Use evidence-based bullets (link PRs) — calibration committee rejects vague notes.

Operational items (people-ops)
----
- People Ops will run cohort calibration every two weeks — bring rubric snapshots.
- For extensions/offboards, use the standard people-ops offboard checklist (link in linked_artifacts).
- Track mentor load: mentors should not carry more than 3 Launchpad mentees concurrently.

Open questions / parking lot
----
- Should we formalize a cohort-wide learning sprint (2 days) focused on infra primers? (Marco to prototype curriculum)
- How many extension weeks are reasonable? (prev practice 30; propose max 60 total with clear milestones)
- Is manager allowed to select mentor from outside team? (yes, but require 1:1 sync cadence and manager approval)

Action items (owners)
----
- Priya: draft short Confluence page summarizing this compact flow (due 2025-07-10).
- Marco: prototype 2-day infra primer deck for cohort (due 2025-07-17).
- Leah: add rubric template to People Ops Google Drive folder and create a copyable doc template (due 2025-07-08).
- Samir: confirm mentor capacity limits and add to People Ops tracker.

Notes to self
----
- Keep language lightweight — managers hate heavy forms early.
- This doc should be a starting checklist; the real artifact is the dossier with links.
- Iterate after three cohorts (capture metrics: time-to-first-PR, percent green at 30, 90-day retention).

References and sample artifacts
----
- example PR: repo/redwood/example-first-pr (link in linked_artifacts)
- sample 30-day rubric (attached in People Ops folder)
- calibration notes: Slack thread and Confluence page above

End of doc: compact, intentionally informal. Use as working template and adapt to role-specific needs.
